# Provenance of `reference-tools.json`

The committed capture is the `tools/list` (and `resources/list`) of the reference
memory server, taken once by hand and reviewed as source. `surface_test.go` compares
this server's published tool contract against it, so the capture is the pin: it is
edited deliberately, with a reviewed diff, never regenerated by the build.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| package | `@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory` |
| version | `2.1.0` (`serverInfo.version` in the capture) |
| upstream | https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers — `src/memory/index.ts` |
| licence | MIT (`src/memory/README.md` §License) |
| captured | 2026-11-06 |
| node | `v26.7.0` |
| negotiated protocol | `2025-11-25` |
| transport | stdio |

## Capture procedure

```sh
export MEMORY_FILE_PATH=$(mktemp -d)/memory.jsonl
npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory
```

then, on stdin, a JSON-RPC `initialize` (`protocolVersion: "2025-11-25"`),
`notifications/initialized`, `tools/list` (id 2) and `resources/list` (id 3), one JSON
object per line; the responses are the capture, unedited.

## Deliberate differences asserted by the test

The test compares **structure**: tool names, titles, annotation hints, argument
and result property names, types, `required` lists, and openness. Descriptions
are excluded, because they are model-facing prose rather than contract. As of
this capture there are no structural differences: argument and result schemas for
all nine tools, the annotations, and the resource metadata are the reference's.

| # | Difference | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Tool descriptions are this server's own wording | Prose is not contract; the test excludes it so wording can be improved without a capture refresh |
| 2 | `create_entities` sends the result as compact JSON plus the skipped-entity notice; the reference sends pretty-printed JSON plus the same notice | The structured content is identical; only the text rendering differs |
| 3 | `serverInfo.name` is `gassaway`; instructions and error wording are this server's | Identity and prose, not the tool contract |
